title: Singer-Songwriter
tagline: Personal songs built around voice, guitar, and a direct point of view.
summary: The singer-songwriter tradition is grounded in directness: one voice, one instrument, and a lyric shaped by lived experience. It draws from folk, blues, pop, and country, creating songs that feel intimate without losing emotional power. The form thrives on confession, interpretation, and a strong sense of character.

pillars.name: Bob Dylan
pillars.why: Bob Dylan expanded the singer-songwriter form into something poetic, political, and endlessly influential.

pillars.name: Joni Mitchell
pillars.why: Joni Mitchell fused lyrical sophistication, guitar craft, and emotional detail into a singular artistic language.

pillars.name: Nick Drake
pillars.why: Nick Drake showed how subtle arrangements and intimate phrasing could create a profound, fragile emotional world.
